messages.content: I need help finishing an event schema migration.
Happy to help with an event schema migration.
Personally one topic per event type rather than a shared bus feels right to me.
Nothing failed on the last run. Checkpointing to durable storage every 30 seconds is no longer on my plate.
That leaves the change data capture connector on the orders table behind us.

Glad to report backpressure handling in the consumer loop is sorted. Between the options, keying events by aggregate ID for ordering came out ahead. Eventually migrating the remaining consumers off the v1 schema has to get done too.

After a couple of tries, exactly-once semantics on the aggregation job finally works. Turned out streams/consumer.py was the culprit file. Once the build is green we can merge. Turned out streams/aggregator.py was the culprit file.
I lean towards at-least-once delivery with idempotent consumers.
Someone should pick up reducing end-to-end latency below one second. docker-compose.yml got a few more lines. Yep, doing that. Nothing failed on the last run.
Eventually a replay procedure for the last 24 hours has to get done too. Kafka over Kinesis for the event backbone is the clear winner here.

That leaves windowed aggregation over five-minute tumbling windows behind us. The topic layout with twelve partitions per stream is no longer on my plate. Decisions like this usually need a design doc.
